key_insight: Sequential thermal evaporation produces different solid-state conversion pathways in wide-bandgap and narrow-bandgap perovskite stacks, so bandgap control must be tailored to each absorber chemistry.
engineering_relevance: This work provides a process design rule for scalable, solvent-free fabrication of all-perovskite tandem solar cells and enables high-efficiency device integration with improved thermal stability.
method: Time-sliced ex situ analysis of sequentially evaporated precursor stacks
Compare conversion behavior in mixed-halide WBG and Sn-Pb NBG absorbers
Use guided absorber optimization to build an evaporated all-perovskite tandem device
evidence_signal: The paper reports bandgaps spanning 1.26-1.96 eV, a first evaporated all-perovskite tandem with 19.2% efficiency, and 80% average retained efficiency after 1,200 h at 65 °C under ISOS-D-2 testing.
watch_item: The conversion pathways are highly chemistry-dependent, so process windows may not transfer directly between WBG and NBG stacks without separate control of precursor thickness, diffusion, and annealing.
paper_title: Divergent Solid-state Conversion Pathways in Evaporated All-perovskite Tandem Solar Cells
